input.quote: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the Fees paid or payable by Customer under the first Order Form during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.
input.rationale: The structure is otherwise strong — the cap is expressly mutual, the exclusion of indirect/consequential damages is mutual, and Excluded Claims already carry all preferred carve-outs (confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement). The defect is the cap basis: "Fees" is defined as the Implementation Fee only, a one-time USD 12,000 charge stated in the first Order Form, so the cap is illusory and far below six months' fees — walk-away territory. For the same reason the payment carve-out, keyed to "Fees", does not exclude Customer's actual payment obligations from damages. We reset the basis to the greater of twelve months' fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms and USD 1,000,000 and align the payment noun to "amounts due", preserving the existing temporal anchor and all carve-outs.

proposal.summary: Cap set at greater of 12 months' fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms and USD 1,000,000; payment carve-out broadened to amounts due.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] "Fees" is defined as the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form, so the cap is illusory; we set it at the greater of twelve months' fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms and USD 1,000,000, and align the payment carve-out to all amounts due. Excluded Claims (confidentiality, data protection and security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement) remain outside the cap.
